Abiathar
uh-BY-uh-thar
noun (proper, person)
Hebrew Ebyathar, "father of abundance" or "my father is great," from ab (father) and yathar (to be abundant, to remain over).

📖 Biblical Definition

Abiathar was the son of Ahimelech the priest of Nob, and the sole survivor of the slaughter that Saul commanded when Doeg the Edomite fell upon the priests for having aided David (1 Sam 22:18-20). Abiathar escaped and fled to David, bringing with him the ephod, and David said unto him, "Abide thou with me, fear not" (1 Sam 22:23). Through David's wilderness years Abiathar inquired of the LORD for him by the ephod, and he shared David's exile and his enthronement, bearing the ark and standing as priest in Jerusalem alongside Zadok. Yet at the last, when Adonijah exalted himself to be king against the LORD's purpose for Solomon, Abiathar took Adonijah's part (1 Kings 1:7). For this Solomon thrust him out from being priest unto the LORD, sparing his life for his faithfulness in David's afflictions, but removing him to his fields at Anathoth (1 Kings 2:26-27). In this the Scripture marks a solemn fulfilment: "that he might fulfil the word of the LORD, which he spake concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh" (1 Kings 2:27), for Abiathar was of Eli's line, and the sentence pronounced against that house was at last accomplished. This dictionary confesses that the word of the LORD standeth sure though it tarry many generations, that long faithfulness does not license a final treason, and that God removes and sets up whom He will, even in the highest offices of His house.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The one priest of Nob who escaped Saul's slaughter and fled to David, serving as his priest. He later sided with Adonijah and was deposed by Solomon, fulfilling the word against Eli's house.

expand to see more

ABIATHAR, noun. Son of Ahimelech, priest of Nob; sole escapee of Saul's massacre and high priest under David.

"And one of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled after David" (1 Sam 22:20).

His office required faithful inquiry of the LORD for the king by the ephod.

He served David long, yet later sided with Adonijah against Solomon, the LORD's chosen.

The sanction: deposed from the priesthood, fulfilling the word spoken against the house of Eli.

📖 Key Scripture

1 Sam 22:20 — "And one of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled after David."

1 Sam 22:23 — "Abide thou with me, fear not: for he that seeketh my life seeketh thy life: but with me thou shalt be in safeguard."

1 Kings 2:26 — "And unto Abiathar the priest said the king, Get thee to Anathoth, unto thine own fields; for thou art worthy of death: but I will not at this time put thee to death, because thou barest the ark of the Lord GOD before David my father, and because thou hast been afflicted in all wherein my father was afflicted."

1 Kings 2:27 — "So Solomon thrust out Abiathar from being priest unto the LORD; that he might fulfil the word of the LORD, which he spake concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Abiathar faces no modern redefinition; his fall recovers the truth that long service cannot purchase a final rebellion, and that God's word against a house is sure.

expand to see more

Abiathar's life is a sober mingling of fidelity and failure. He bore the ark, suffered exile, and inquired faithfully for David through years of danger; no man could question his loyalty in the day of trouble. Yet at the end he chose the wrong king, casting his lot with Adonijah's self-exaltation rather than with Solomon whom the LORD had named. His mercy from Solomon's hand was real, but so was his removal.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the word of the LORD, here the sentence on Eli's house spoken generations before, comes infallibly to pass. A man may serve God's anointed long and still forfeit his office by a late treason; perseverance is proved at the end, not merely begun at the start. God's purposes for His true King will not be overthrown by any priest's misjudgment.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From Hebrew Ebyathar, "father of abundance," the priest who survived Nob and served David.

expand to see more

Hebrew Ebyathar joins ab, father, with the root yathar, to remain over or abound.

He carried the ephod, the priestly garment used to inquire of the LORD.

Of the house of Eli through Ahitub, he stood under the ancient sentence on that line.

Anathoth, his place of banishment, was a Levitical city in Benjamin (Josh 21:18).

Zadok his colleague held the office that passed wholly to his line after Abiathar fell.

Usage

"Abiathar alone escaped the sword of Doeg and fled with the ephod to David in the cave."

"When Adonijah seized the kingdom, Abiathar followed and helped him, to his own undoing."

"Solomon's deposing of Abiathar fulfilled to the letter the word long before spoken against Eli."
